runs.title: GLASS mocks, tomographic
runs.stale_note: These mocks match the first calibrated sample's tomographic footprint (4,065 deg²). An ensemble on the current footprint (4,582 deg²) is being generated.
runs.summary: Each chip asks whether the 69 mock PTEs of one joint B-mode test are uniform, which they are when the analytic covariance describes the scatter of the mocks. It does for Cℓ BB, Cℓ EB and ξ− B (12–83′); for COSEBIs B, ξ+ B (12–83′), ξ± B (12–83′) and ξ± B (2–20′) the mocks scatter 6–10% more than the analytic covariance says (mean χ²/dof 1.06–1.10), so those tests' analytic PTEs read slightly low on the data too. The mocks are matched to the data cell's bins and n(z). The blinded data's Cℓ BB additive-template amplitude, 0.77 ± 0.22, lies 3.3σ above the mock mean, with 0 of 69 mocks higher; we read this as an additive B-mode systematic in the data, which mocks without systematics do not produce.
runs.banner: GLASS mocks under a throwaway blind; the input cosmology is known. The data B modes shown against them are blinded data, which the blind leaves unchanged
runs.lacks: Sampled mocks have unit weights, Gaussian shape noise at the data's per-bin σ_e and n_eff, no PSF leakage and no additive B mode, so this run has no PSF section.
provenance: GLASS sampled mocks on the v2 tomographic footprint (4,065 deg²), 69 of 69 seeds, nside 4096, each bin's n_eff and σ_e from the data

runs.headline_note: Covariance checks: KS p-value that the 69 mock PTEs of each joint B-mode test are uniform, as they are when the analytic covariance describes the mock scatter

tables.caption: Each joint B-mode test runs over all ten bin pairs on every mock, against the analytic covariance. A PTE (probability to exceed) is the chance that pure noise gives a χ² at least this large. Mean mock χ²/dof is 1 and the median PTE 0.5 when the analytic covariance describes the mock scatter; about 3.5 mocks per test fall below 0.05 by chance.
Joint B-mode null tests of the blinded data over all ten bin pairs. The rescaled PTE multiplies the analytic covariance by the mocks' mean χ²/dof; the last column counts mocks directly.

columns.label: data PTE, covariance rescaled to the mocks

tables.caption: χ² ignores sign; an additive B mode (PSF leakage, a shared shear offset) pushes B modes the same way across scales and pairs. The template amplitude A is the least-squares fit of C_BB = A × 2.6×10⁻¹¹ exp[−(ℓ/2000)²] to Cℓ BB with the analytic covariance; the mean data/σ averages each element over its analytic standard deviation. The mocks have no additive B, so they give each number's null distribution.

runs.title: GLASS mock, non-tomographic
runs.stale_note: No cosmo_val run on a non-tomographic v2 mock has finished. The painted suite on Nibi (clean, blinded, PSF-leakage and additive-B twins) stopped at 39 of 74 steps on 1 Nov and was resumed on 10 Nov. Until it lands, this cell shows how the mock is built, not its null tests.
runs.summary: One painted mock exists and its construction is checked: the sky matches its input spectrum (mean ratio 0.998 over ℓ = 100–8000) and a pure-E sky reads as pure E (BB/EE = 7e-09). Its null tests are not measured yet.
runs.banner: GLASS mock with a known input cosmology; no data vector is shown
runs.lacks: Source clustering correlated with the lensing field. PSF leakage is absent unless injected: each galaxy keeps its real PSF but gets a random orientation.
provenance: GLASS seed 1 painted on ShapePipe SP v2.0, upper bound 9 on galaxy size relative to the PSF (170,617,249 galaxies): real positions, weights and |e|, random orientations
none applied: these figures compare the mock with its own input

figures.caption: The full-sky convergence and E-mode spectra of the seed-1 GLASS sky against the input theory. The ratio stays at 1 up to ℓ = 8000; a pixel lookup at nside 4096 would follow the dotted curve.
figures.alt: The full-sky convergence and E-mode spectra of the seed-1 GLASS sky against the input theory. The ratio stays at 1 up to ℓ = 8000; a pixel lookup at nside 4096 would follow the dotted curve.

figures.caption: The painted catalogue against its inputs, on one million galaxies: the |e| distribution is unchanged by the random rotation, the saved shear equals the sky at each position, and the mean painted ellipticity follows the true shear with slope 1.
figures.alt: The painted catalogue against its inputs, on one million galaxies: the |e| distribution is unchanged by the random rotation, the saved shear equals the sky at each position, and the mean painted ellipticity follows the true shear with slope 1.

figures.caption: A pure-E sky measured with the pipeline's pseudo-Cℓ estimator. With the catalogue's polarisation convention it reads as pure E; with the opposite sign it reads as mixed E and B.
figures.alt: A pure-E sky measured with the pipeline's pseudo-Cℓ estimator. With the catalogue's polarisation convention it reads as pure E; with the opposite sign it reads as mixed E and B.
